title: Russian FSB Responds After U.S. Warns of Imminent Terrorist Threat in Moscow
snippet: Russian security forces are taking action following a U.S. Embassy warning about a potential mass casualty event at Moscow's Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve.
content:
MOSCOW — Russian security forces are taking action in response to an urgent intelligence warning from the U.S. Embassy regarding a potential terrorist attack in Moscow, officials confirmed Saturday.

The U.S. Embassy issued a security alert stating it was aware of a credible threat involving a possible mass casualty event targeting the Tsaritsyno Museum Reserve, a popular imperial palace and park complex located in southern Moscow. U.S. officials advised individuals to avoid the area, remain alert, and stay away from crowds, noting that Washington is coordinating its response with Russian authorities.

Security Lockdown at Tsaritsyno Park

Following the alert, Russian security personnel deployed to the Tsaritsyno complex. According to Baza, a Russian Telegram channel linked to law enforcement, the park was closed to new visitors and restricted to exits only while officers inspected the premises.

Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) confirmed receiving information from the U.S. government regarding the preparation of a terrorist attack, stating that 'appropriate work is underway.'

A History of U.S. Warnings

The embassy did not release details on who was plotting the alleged attack. However, the sharing of intelligence between Washington and Moscow highlights a crucial, if rare, channel of communication despite current geopolitical strain.

The U.S. government has previously alerted Moscow to imminent threats. In March 2024, American intelligence warned Russian officials of a planned strike weeks before ISIS-K terrorists attacked the Crocus City Hall concert venue outside Moscow, an attack that killed more than 140 people.
